text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
I'm working through the payoff structure of this public goods game—keeping a token privately gives me 1 point but costs each other member 0.3, while putting a token in the group account seems to pay me 0.3 points per token, and I need to figure out whether it also benefits others or just me.

Working through the math either way, keeping tokens privately still dominates individually since others' contributions don't depend on my choice, even though mutual cooperation would yield a better social outcome. Given the repeated 10-round structure, pure self-interest points toward defecting, but I'll weigh whether signaling cooperation early has value before settling on an answer of 0.

reply.thinking:

If everyone contributes fully across all 10 rounds, each person nets 6 per round, versus the individually dominant strategy of keeping everything private. Since this is repeated and I don't know the other players, I'm leaning toward opening with full cooperation (contributing all 20) as a signal, though I recognize this is risky if others free-ride and keep everything for themselves.

So everyone defecting nets 20 each, while full cooperation nets 24 each — better for the group but risky if others defect, since cooperating while others defect costs me 14 points. Given it's a repeated game, I'm leaning toward reciprocity-based strategy: for round 1, rather than risking full cooperation or full defection, I'll contribute a moderate amount, maybe around 10, as a signal to test others' willingness to cooperate.
